messages:
jessica_cs: Heads-up — getting escalations from 3 customers about sudden 429s after yesterday's rate policy push. They started ~09:12 UTC and coincide with a small traffic spike. Samples attached below.

ryan_sre: Ugh. Which policy exactly changed? can you paste the policy name/flag?

jessica_cs: It was the new quota window change -> ratepolicy-v2 with adaptive burst enabled. Ops note shows rollout batch 3/10. Repro from customer request: 

```
curl -i -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \ 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ 
  'https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/generate' 
# response headers:
# HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
# x-rw-rate-limit: 750
# x-rw-remaining: 0
# x-rw-reset: 24
```

jessica_cs: They also pasted a trace with per-route p95 latency jump to 700ms concurrently. Not all customers affected, looks correlated to heavy short-lived bursts (chat playgrounds, chatbots doing simultaneous reloads).

liam_platform: Can we see the rollout timeline? I want to know which hosts got the new config. Any chance a misconfigured burst window (ms vs s) slipped through?

deploy-bot: Deploy event: ratepolicy-v2 rollout batch=3/10 triggered by liam_platform at 2026-11-03T09:10:12Z. Canary metrics: init ok.

ryan_sre: If canary metrics were "ok" but real traffic has different burstiness, we should pause rollout and rollback the flag for the remaining hosts. Can someone run a quick query for x-rw-remaining=0 spikes by customer?

jessica_cs: Query results (sample): 
- cust-a: 174 429s in 10m
- cust-b: 48 429s in 15m
- cust-c: 12 429s in 20m

emily_prod: Billing question: did quota units decrement correctly? Are customers being charged for throttled tokens? We need to confirm before we do a rollback to avoid double-billing corrections.

liam_platform: Quick config snippet that was rolled: 
```
{
  "policy_name": "ratepolicy-v2",
  "rules": [{
    "route": "v1/generate",
    "requests_per_minute": 4500,
    "burst": 1800,
    "window_ms": 60000,
    "backoff": "adaptive"
  }]
}
```

liam_platform: I'm suspicious of the window_ms field — if someone accidentally used seconds (60000 vs 60) in a typed config, it could have massively increased allowed burst then the adaptive backoff kicked in incorrectly. Need to confirm exact value on hosts.

ryan_sre: OK. Action plan: (1) pause rollout immediately for remaining batches, (2) run canary rollback on batch 3 hosts, (3) gather 30m post-rollback metrics and check customer 429/latency. I'll take (2). Jessica, can you open a support case per customer and ask for request IDs for repro?

jessica_cs: On it. I'll ask for request ids + exact client lib versions. Also flagged all affected customers with "escalation" priority.

ratepolicy-bot: Policy change detected: ratepolicy-v2 applied to host group "us-east-2-cluster-7". Feature flag: enabled=true.

emily_prod: For billing: we should snapshot token usage in the 15m window before rollback and again after — ops if you can dump usage counters to S3 I can check billing joins.

liam_platform: Command to rollback flag via ops API (use only for canary hosts):
```
curl -X POST https://ops-api.redwood-inference.example/featureflag/toggle \
  -d '{"flag":"ratepolicy-v2","enable":false,"scope":"host:us-east-2-cluster-7"}' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <ops-token>'
```

ryan_sre: I'm running that now on 3 hosts in the batch. Will post results. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

ryan_sre: Rollback applied to batch-hosts: host-a, host-b, host-c. Reconfig reload triggered. Observability notes: p95 latency dropping, 429 counts for cust-a down by ~85% in last 4m.

jessica_cs: Customer cust-a confirms fewer 429s and chat sessions resuming. :white_check_mark:

emily_prod: Billing snapshot saved to s3://ops-snapshots/ratepolicy-v2/2026-11-03T09:30Z. I'll validate counters and follow up with finance.

liam_platform: We'll freeze the rollout and do a postmortem tomorrow. Immediate follow-ups: fix config validation to reject ms/seconds mismatch, add a canary test that simulates heavy short bursts (reloads from multiple users), and add a per-customer burst cap so a single tenant doesn't exhaust shared buckets.

ryan_sre: Agreed. For now we'll keep ratepolicy-v1 active for all remaining clusters and re-run a staged rollout with adjusted burst=600 and window_ms=60000 in a smaller canary.

jessica_cs: Closing the support escalation for the three customers that confirmed recovery. I'll keep the thread updated if anything else pops up. Thanks everyone. :pray:

ratepolicy-bot: Rollout paused: remaining batches cancelled.

liam_platform: Postmortem doc: https://confluence.redwood-inference.example/display/OPS/2026-11-03+-+RatepolicyV2+Burst+Incident (draft)

ryan_sre: Follow-up task list created in ops board. I'll ping when the new canary is scheduled.
